chunks: If they break their oaths after their covenant and revile your faith, then fight the leaders of disbelief; indeed, they have no oaths [to keep], so perhaps they will desist.
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'leaders of disbelief' mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah and why should they be fought?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the breach of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah by the Quraysh, establishing the principle of active defense against treaty-breakers. It highlights that the leaders of disbelief (A'immah al-Kufr) are the primary targets, as their oaths lack divine sanction, thereby justifying military action to restore religious integrity and deter further aggression.
